### AQUAVEIN-SAR – Project Summary

AQUAVEIN-SAR is an interactive web platform developed to investigate and visualize potential submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) areas, where freshwater naturally flows from coastal aquifers into the ocean. Our project explores how Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology and NASA Earth observation resources can support the investigation of environmental processes in coastal regions.

The platform combines an interactive 3D Earth model, satellite visualizations, geographic exploration tools, and an engineering simulation. We have also created a downloadable digital magazine to make scientific information and project findings more accessible to students, researchers, and the wider public.

As climate change, drought, and freshwater scarcity increasingly threaten global water security, exploring alternative freshwater resources is essential. AQUAVEIN-SAR aims to support research into potential submarine freshwater sources and contribute to more sustainable water resource management.

AQUAVEIN-SAR – Detailed Project Description

1. What Does Our Project Do and How Does It Work?

AQUAVEIN-SAR is an interactive web-based research and visualization platform designed to explore potential Submarine Groundwater Discharge (SGD) areas, where freshwater naturally flows from coastal aquifers into the sea.

Our platform brings together satellite-based observations, geographic information, environmental indicators, and interactive simulations. Inspired by NASA's NISAR mission and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology, the project explores how satellite observations can support the investigation of coastal environments and potential freshwater pathways.

The platform offers several interactive features:

  • Interactive 3D Earth: Users can explore the globe and examine selected ocean and coastal locations.
  • SAR Satellite Visualization: Satellite-themed visualizations introduce radar observation concepts and their potential use in environmental research.
  • Geographic Exploration: Users can explore selected coastal and ocean locations and examine information about potential groundwater discharge areas.
  • Step-by-Step Simulation: An interactive simulation illustrates the conceptual process from satellite observation to potential site identification and underwater investigation.
  • Engineering and Extraction Simulator: Users can experiment with parameters such as pump flow rate, pipe diameter, and system configuration to understand the engineering considerations of a hypothetical extraction system.
  • Digital E-Magazine: A six-page downloadable publication presents scientific information, project findings, and educational content. It is designed to be updated periodically as new information and analyses become available.
  • QR Code Accessibility: QR codes provide quick access to the web platform and digital magazine.

AQUAVEIN-SAR is an exploratory and educational prototype. SAR satellites do not directly image freshwater beneath the seafloor. Instead, satellite observations can provide environmental information that may help researchers investigate potential areas. Actual groundwater discharge and water quality must be verified through field measurements and hydrogeological studies.

2. What Benefits Does It Provide?

Freshwater scarcity is becoming an increasingly important global challenge due to climate change, drought, population growth, and increasing water demand.

AQUAVEIN-SAR aims to make research on potential submarine freshwater resources more accessible by combining satellite observations, geographic visualization, and interactive educational tools in one platform.

Its main benefits include:

  • Raising awareness about freshwater scarcity and alternative freshwater resources.
  • Making satellite observation concepts easier to understand.
  • Providing an interactive environment for exploring coastal and ocean regions.
  • Supporting preliminary research and the planning of future field investigations.
  • Making scientific information accessible through a downloadable digital magazine.
  • Encouraging students and researchers to explore the relationship between space technology, hydrology, and environmental sustainability.

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

Our long-term vision is to support scientific exploration of potential submarine freshwater resources and contribute to discussions about sustainable water management.

By making satellite-based observations and research information easier to explore, AQUAVEIN-SAR aims to connect space technology with one of humanity's most important needs: access to freshwater.

The project does not claim to extract or purify water directly. Instead, it provides a preliminary research and visualization environment that could help guide future scientific investigations.

4. Tools, Technologies, and Resources

The project was developed as a web-based digital prototype. Its main components include:

  • NASA NISAR Mission Resources: Research background on L-band and S-band SAR technology.
  • NASA Earthdata: A reference portal for exploring NASA Earth observation datasets.
  • NISAR Data Products: Scientific and technical reference materials related to satellite observations.
  • NASA SWOT Mission Resources: Reference information on ocean surface height and surface water observations.
  • Interactive 3D Visualization: A digital globe for geographic exploration.
  • Web-Based Simulation: Interactive controls for exploring hypothetical engineering and extraction-system parameters.
  • Digital Publishing Tools: Creation of a six-page electronic magazine.
  • QR Code Technology: Direct access to the website and digital publication.
  • GitHub and Cloud Deployment: Project documentation, version management, and online access to the prototype.

The specific programming languages, frameworks, and hardware components are not identified in the project documentation. The prototype's confirmed implementation is primarily software- and web-based.

5. What Makes Our Project Creative and Innovative?

The creative aspect of AQUAVEIN-SAR is the combination of space-based observation concepts, groundwater research, interactive geographic visualization, and engineering simulation in a single educational platform.

Rather than presenting satellite data only as static maps or technical reports, we transform the research concept into an interactive experience. Users can explore a 3D Earth model, examine coastal locations, follow a conceptual detection process, experiment with engineering parameters, and access scientific information through a digital magazine.

This multidisciplinary approach connects space science, remote sensing, hydrology, environmental awareness, and engineering.

6. Factors Considered by Our Team

During the development process, our team considered:

  • The growing global need for freshwater resources.
  • The importance of coastal aquifers and submarine groundwater discharge.
  • The capabilities and limitations of SAR satellite observations.
  • The need to distinguish potential indicators from scientifically verified groundwater sources.
  • The accessibility of scientific information for students, researchers, and the wider public.
  • The importance of an interactive, understandable, and visually engaging user experience.
  • The need for field validation and hydrogeological assessment before any real-world extraction decision.

Our Vision:

From Satellite Observations to Groundwater Discovery — Exploring Hidden Water Pathways for a More Sustainable Future.
